question: What's the best e-learning content library for leadership development programs?
text:
If you mean a ready-made content library that you can plug into a corporate leadership-development program, there isn't one universally “best” choice—the right fit depends on whether you prioritize breadth, leadership depth, learning experience, localization, or LMS integration.

Here’s how I’d shortlist the major options:

Library	Particularly strong for	Leadership content	Breadth	Best fit
LinkedIn Learning	Broad leadership + business skills	Very broad	★★★★★	Organizations wanting one library for many employee populations
Skillsoft Percipio	Structured leadership development	Very deep	★★★★☆	Formal leadership academies and manager programs
GoodHabitz	Practical, accessible soft-skills learning	Strong	★★★★☆	European organizations and high-volume employee development
My take

For a general-purpose corporate leadership program, I'd start with LinkedIn Learning. Its current library has more than 26,000 courses overall, with 3,900+ experts, 20+ subtitle languages and 1,300+ curated learning paths. Its leadership catalogue covers areas such as leading teams, executive presence, strategic thinking, feedback, coaching, change and inclusive leadership.

LinkedIn
+1

For a dedicated leadership academy, I'd investigate Skillsoft Percipio very seriously. Its experience is more explicitly organized around structured development: Aspire Journeys, leadership-specific journeys, live learning, simulations, books/audiobooks and skill benchmarking are all part of the ecosystem.

documentation.skillsoft.com

For a European workforce where accessibility, localization and practical soft skills matter, GoodHabitz is particularly interesting. Its library is available in 20+ languages and includes leadership, teamwork, wellbeing and digital skills, with new content added monthly.
